title: The Hilbert scheme of degree-$d$ divisors on a curve is geometrically integral
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a curve over $k$ [def-pc-curve] which is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] over $k$ and geometrically irreducible over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $d\geq0$ and let $H_d$ be a scheme over $k$ representing [def-pc-representable-functor] the functor $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{X/k}$ [def-pc-hilb-functor]. Then $H_d$ is geometrically integral over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]: for every field extension $k'/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] the base change $H_d\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-base-change] is an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme].

source.place: Tag 0B9I (proposition-hilb-d), proof of (1): 'Since X is geometrically irreducible over k, the product X^d is irreducible (Varieties, Lemma 038F) hence the image is irreducible (in fact geometrically irreducible)', with smoothness of H_d (Lemma 0B9H) for geometric reducedness (Varieties 056T); Lean: WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Hilbert.Curve, AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_and_geometricallyIntegral_of_representableBy_hilbertPresheaf_curve, lines 1079-1105 (second conjunct; slopmaster2 71d63dcf)

proof.text: By [thm-pc-hilb-curves] (1), every functor $\operatorname{Hilb}^e_{X/k}$ is representable; the given representing scheme $H_d$ is isomorphic to the representing scheme in that theorem. Hence $H_d\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth by [lem-pc-hilb-smooth]. Applying [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] directly to this morphism (whose only fibre is $H_d$) shows that $H_d$ is geometrically reduced, i.e. $H_{d,k'}$ is reduced for every field extension $k'/k$.

source.place: Tag 0B9I, proof of (1), smoothness and Varieties Lemma 056T

proof.text: First, $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth, so [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] gives geometric reducedness of $X$: for every $k'/k$, $X_{k'}$ is reduced [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Since $X$ is a nonempty curve [def-pc-curve] and is geometrically irreducible, [def-pc-integral-scheme] makes each $X_{k'}$ integral; thus $X$ is geometrically integral. For each extension $k'/k$, apply [lem-sc-hilb-dominating-power] to obtain $Y\to H_d$ with $Y$ geometrically irreducible over $k$. The morphism $Y_{k'}\to H_{d,k'}$ is the base change of $\pi$ along $H_{d,k'}\to H_d$ (because $\pi$ followed by $H_d\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $q$), hence is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. The base change $Y_{k'}$ is irreducible by geometric irreducibility, so its surjective continuous image $H_{d,k'}$ is irreducible.

source.place: Tag 0B9I, proof of (1): X^d is geometrically irreducible by Varieties Lemma 038F and its surjective image is irreducible

proof.text: A scheme that is both reduced and irreducible is integral. Applying this to every $H_{d,k'}$ proves that $H_d$ is geometrically integral over $k$. Each $H_{d,k'}$ is nonempty because it is irreducible (equivalently, because the surjection from the nonempty $Y_{k'}$ has image $H_{d,k'}$).
